This path is the direct chain used only by proof/src/bin/live_turn.rs, not the shipped broker. R2-0132 records the same defect, but at engine/ci/live/run_ladder_supervisor.py:243, not at this path.

evidence: `let _ = child.kill(); let _ = child.wait();` under the comment "Do not let an unrecorded execution run to completion behind its back". `child` is recorder_command[0], which the kit requires to be sudo (run_live_turn.sh:458); SIGKILL to sudo is not relayed and no process group is set. Reasoned, not run.
suggested_fix: Spawn the recorder in its own process group and signal the group through a path the recorder uid honours, or have the supervisor's refusal stop the attempt.
title: A refused `execution-started` kills only the sudo invoker, not the recorder/launcher/executor it started
verify: chain_executor.rs:1033-1034 calls child.kill() on recorder_command[0], which the kit requires to be sudo (run_live_turn.sh:456-458), and no setsid/process_group/killpg appears in the file, so the signal targets the sudo pid alone. Whether the recorder and executor survive was not run (no sudo here) and depends on sudo's pty setting; the path is built only by the proof driver. R2-0132 records the adjacent pid-is-not-a-group defect at a different path.

evidence: `pub fn to_turn_reason(&self) -> TurnReason { TurnReason::UpstreamBlocked }` ignores self; hop_request maps every HopError through it. `HopError::Refused(String)` is constructed at L78 and its string is read nowhere in broker/src outside tests, so a `blocked` reply cannot say which hop refused or why.
suggested_fix: Log the principal and reason on stderr in hop_request before collapsing to UpstreamBlocked.
title: A principal's typed refusal reason is parsed and then discarded without being logged
verify: chain_hops.rs:37-39 `to_turn_reason(&self)` returns TurnReason::UpstreamBlocked unconditionally, and hop_request (chain_executor.rs:381-383) maps every HopError through it with no eprintln. grep for `Refused` in broker/src finds only the constructor at L78 and a test at L150, so the principal's reason string is read nowhere; a diagnostic gap, not a wrong verdict.

evidence: `.map(|m| m.values().filter_map(|v| v.as_u64().map(|u| u as u32)).collect()).unwrap_or_default()` — a non-integer uid is skipped, a value above u32::MAX wraps, and a missing `uids` block yields an empty principal list. L340: "Fail-closed in every direction".
suggested_fix: Return fail_closed() when `uids` is absent, or any entry is not an integer that fits u32.
title: Malformed or oversized `uids` entries are silently dropped or truncated before the TCB floor, in a block that claims to fail closed in every direction
verify: apps/desktop/src-tauri/broker/src/main.rs:343-347 is exactly as cited: `filter_map(|v| v.as_u64().map(|u| u as u32))` then `unwrap_or_default()`, so a non-integer uid is skipped, a value above u32::MAX wraps, and an absent `uids` block leaves only login_uid in the principal set handed to verify_broker_tcb. Nothing in main.rs refuses those cases (preflight.rs:710-714 repeats the same cast); R2-0809 is a different defect at provision_keys.py.

evidence: The only write to the cell is line 399-401 `*cell = Some((verified, ...))` after all checks; no path sets None. Doc :423-425 says 'no turn has resolved keys yet, or the last one failed a check ... returns NoTrustedManifest'. Tests (:627, :964, :1093) only fail the FIRST turn.
suggested_fix: Set the cell to None at the top of resolve_keys (before any check) and add a test that succeeds once, then fails a persist, and asserts NoTrustedManifest.
title: The custody observation is never cleared, so a turn that fails after an earlier success leaves the earlier observation in place
verify: manifest_resolver.rs:399-401 is the only write to the custody cell and nothing sets None, so the doc at :423 ('or the last one failed a check ... returns NoTrustedManifest') is false after an earlier success. No wrong commit follows today: ladder_executor.rs:341 returns on resolve_keys failure before custody is consulted and the manifest is process-static, so this is a false doc sentence plus an untested latent state, not a reachable bug.

evidence: :399 `if let Ok(mut cell) = p.custody.lock() { *cell = Some(...) }` — on a poisoned mutex nothing is recorded and no error is returned; the turn proceeds and is later refused at commit with 'no turn has verified a manifest', while the floor lock two steps earlier (:383) maps poison to UpstreamBlocked.
suggested_fix: Map the lock error to TurnReason::UpstreamBlocked, as the floor lock does.
title: A poisoned custody lock is swallowed and resolve_keys still returns Ok
verify: manifest_resolver.rs:399-401 is `if let Ok(mut cell) = p.custody.lock() { ... }` with no else, whereas the floor lock at :383 maps poison to UpstreamBlocked. On poison the turn continues and BrokerCustody::resolve (:436-442) returns NoTrustedManifest('no turn has verified a manifest under a pinned anchor yet'), so it fails closed with a misleading reason; an inconsistency, not a trust break.

evidence: preflight.rs:712-714 'if let Some(u) = v.as_u64() { uids.insert(u as u32); }' — a string uid is skipped and 4294967296 becomes 0. tcb_verify.rs uid(): 'u32::try_from(u).ok().filter(|u| *u != u32::MAX)' else an error.

title: Preflight's uid_set truncates and drops uids the way the fixed parser refuses
verify: preflight.rs:707-716 uid_set does `if let Some(u) = v.as_u64() { uids.insert(u as u32); }`: a non-integer is skipped and an out-of-range value truncates, while proof/src/tcb_verify.rs uid() uses u32::try_from and rejects u32::MAX, with a doc comment naming exactly these two behaviours as the removed defect. Effect is confined to two preflight report rows (check_seven_accounts, check_floor_covers_sidecar); a dropped uid still fails the count of seven, a truncated one could be counted as uid 0. Not found in either read file.

evidence: :714 `uids.insert(u as u32)` from as_u64; :770, :1110, :1310 `cfg.i(&["uids","broker"]).map(|u| u as u32)` from i64 (-1 becomes 4294967295; 4294972297 becomes 5001); :936 same for supervisor. main.rs:345 does the same cast.

title: Config uids are narrowed with `as u32`, so an out-of-range or negative value silently becomes another uid

evidence: :825 `pin.artifacts.iter().find(|a| a.logical_name == "privileged-launcher.bin")`. check_root_custody uses `pin.sole_artifact(ROOT_ANCHOR_ROLE)` (:1362) and the ledger lookup refuses two names ('will not choose one', :916-923).

evidence: check_floor_custody (:1102-1130) stats only trust.floor_path. key_manifest.rs:433-440 write_floor_atomically creates `path.with_extension("json.tmp")` and renames; a broker-owned 0600 floor in a directory the broker cannot write reads MET while every turn refuses. evidence: :1152-1153 `match host.stat(&path) { Some(_) => Status::met(format!("{path} exists"))` — the mode is not read, so a regular file or directory at that path reports MET for 'names the challenge authority's AF_UNIX socket, and it is there' (:279).

evidence: check_resolved (:1253-1273) demands resolved.run_id/task_id/requested_at_ms; row text :320-324 says 'an empty one is signed ... inside a real receipt'. evidence: L13 'added_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))'. repo.rs:1599-1600 inserts added_at = now() (epoch ms string). A row written through the default would sort and compare differently from every other timestamp in the database.

evidence: L169-174 'Bumped 1 -> 2 ... a v1 and a v2 grant are different objects'. verify() L520-527 parses the grant and checks only writer and expiry; L532-536 checks only step count for the flow. L188 still writes artifact_type "brops.agent-grant.v1" beside schema 2. A v1 grant with egress [] parses and is accepted.

verify: verify() L520-537 parses the grant and flow and checks only writer, expiry and step count; grant.schema, flow.schema and every artifact_type are never read, and for_local_only L187-188 writes schema 2 beside artifact_type 'brops.agent-grant.v1'. evidence: L534 'flow.steps.len() as u32 > flow.max_steps' compares the flow against a number read from the same flow.json (L119). A flow declaring max_steps 4294967295 passes; the runner (repo.rs:3201) loops over all steps with no limit of its own.

evidence: L516 'The digest of the bytes the SIDECAR served'; L519 'served_b64.as_ref().map(|b| sha256_hex(b.as_bytes()))' where served_b64 is the bytes_b64 string. A reader comparing it to a chunk digest of the output would never match.

verify: L504 served_b64 is the reply's bytes_b64 string and L519 hashes b.as_bytes() of that text, under the key served_chunk_sha256 and a comment calling it the digest of the bytes served. Nothing in the repo consumes the field, so it is a naming/evidence defect only.

evidence: L171-172 'serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&r.get::<_, String>(4)?).unwrap_or(serde_json::Value::Null)' — the receipts.jsonl the gate reads would show null for a corrupt receipt and the binary would still exit 0.

evidence: L138 'let _ = broker_turns::settle(conn, &broker_turn_id, TurnState::Committed);' then returns committed. L88 expire_stale_live flips ANY live row older than 300_000 ms to 'blocked' (broker_turns.rs:305, not scoped to the conversation); settle then returns NotLive, which is thrown away.

verify: broker_orchestrator.rs L138 is 'let _ = broker_turns::settle(.., Committed)' after persist_committed succeeded; settle (broker_turns.rs:272-288) returns NotLive when the row is no longer live, and expire_stale_live (L302-308) flips every live row older than 300000 ms to blocked with no conversation scope. The test at L880-889 asserts only is_err(). Acknowledged in the comment, so a labelling defect, not an acceptance one.

evidence: L138-142: tx.execute("DELETE FROM credential_bindings WHERE ...")?; audit::record(tx, "credential.unbound", ...). The affected-row count is discarded, so the audit trail states an unbinding that did not happen.

evidence: L80-119 migrate() only applies missing versions 1..26 and never compares the ledger's maximum with SCHEMA_VERSION. grep: SCHEMA_VERSION and current_version( appear only in core/src/lib.rs:113,241 (tests) and core/tests/schema_migrations.rs.

verify: db.rs:76-121 applies only missing versions 1..26 and never compares the ledger's maximum with SCHEMA_VERSION, so a ledger holding version 27 opens silently. evidence: L45-47: 'CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS leaves an older table's stricter constraint in place, so a database created before this change rejects a demonstration_custody row until it is recreated.' The INSERT error is mapped to CommitReadbackMismatch at L150.

evidence: L93-94: readback_trust_state == expected_trust_state && COMMITTABLE_TRUST_STATES.contains(...). evidence: broker/src/ladder_executor.rs:359-360: `resolve_governed_generation_config_v1b().map_err(|_| TurnReason::UpstreamBlocked)?` and l.369 the same for prepare. evidence: L443 `std::fs::rename(&tmp, path)` succeeds, then L450-452 `File::open(dir).and_then(|d| d.sync_all()).map_err(...)?` returns Err. check_and_persist doc L403: "as one operation that cannot be half-done". Disk holds the advance; the caller keeps the old floor.

verify: lib.rs:62-68 maps a clock error to 0 and returns "0", a one-character string under a doc promising fixed 13-digit width; it is reachable only with a system clock before 1970. governed_verification.rs:2043-2046 names this shape as a defect. evidence: L352,354: `unwrap_or(SubjectKind::MemoryEntry)` / `unwrap_or(WriteOp::Updated)` with comment "makes `check_chain` fail loudly". check_chain (L504-560) hashes the substituted value and has no domain check, so 'updated'->'blessed' still recomputes. record_break L464 has the check; its doc L451 says "same three checks".
suggested_fix: Give check_chain the same raw-token domain check record_break makes, or make map() return an error for an unknown token.

evidence: 'if signature_b64.len() > 128 { return Err(ReceiptError::BadSignatureLength(signature_b64.len())); }' while the variant reads 'crypto: signature is {0} bytes, expected 64' (line 146) and line 390 uses it for decoded bytes.

evidence: 'match msg.split("__dup__").nth(1) { Some(rest) => ... ReceiptError::DuplicateKey(...)'. serde_json echoes input in type errors, e.g. the top-level JSON string "__dup__x" gives 'invalid type: string "__dup__x", expected a flat JSON object...', which is reported as DuplicateKey instead of BadJson.

evidence: 'if map.get(*f).unwrap().parse::<u64>().is_err() { return Err(ReceiptError::NotTimestamp(f)); }' — Rust's u64 FromStr accepts a leading '+' and leading zeros, so completed_at:"+2000" passes as 'a millisecond timestamp' and is compared numerically at :527; requested_at is string-bound, completed_at is not.

evidence: :177 'a hostile or runaway error string can never bloat SQLite or the renderer'. record() stores ev.error = ReceiptError::to_string() unbounded: UnknownField(key), BadDecisionDomain(value), Protocol(..), KeyIdMismatch{claimed} carry up to ~64 KiB of envelope text. bounded_reason is called only at commands.rs:1722 (transport).

evidence: in_immediate_tx: 'value: "verify_and_record_receipt must own its transaction; it was called inside an open transaction"'. The same helper serves verify_and_record_held_answer (line 174) and record_pre_verification_block (line 216).

evidence: Doc: "Case-insensitive substring search over title, body, and tags"; the query is `title LIKE ?1 ESCAPE '\\' OR body LIKE ...`. SQLite's built-in LIKE is case-insensitive for ASCII letters only, so Armenian and Russian text (the product's primary languages) matches case-sensitively.

evidence: fail_step_execution only runs `UPDATE run_steps SET status = 'failed'` and returns; complete_step_execution records `run_step.executed` (2184), reconcile records `execution.abandoned` (2244), rejection records `run_step.rejected` (2349). commands.rs:2128 calls it as `let _ = ...` and records nothing either.

verify: fail_step_execution (repo.rs:2197-2210) only runs the UPDATE to 'failed' with no audit::record, while complete_step_execution (2184), reconcile (2244) and rejection (2349) each record one; commands.rs:2125-2131 calls it as `let _ =` and records nothing. evidence: set_step_status takes no Actor; for status == "done" on a gated step it calls approved_for then `consume_for` (2315-2320) and updates the row, with no audit::record anywhere in the function. It is reachable from the renderer through commands.rs:1142 set_run_step_status.

evidence: Only the first active step is completed (2418-2422); the comment says "any other active step stays active and gets its own gate on the next advance()". But if no pending step remains the `None` arm sets succeeded/failed (2461-2462, commented "No active or pending step remains"), and advance then refuses a terminated run (2366).

evidence: `let (outcome, detail) = execute_action(conn, &automation.action)?;` commits its own task/note/notification; the automation_runs INSERT is a later, separate `super::atomic` (2694). If that insert fails, list_runs finds no last run, `due` stays true (2797) and the action repeats every 60s.

title: automations::run commits the action before, and separately from, the run-log row that marks it as run
verify: repo.rs:2691 execute_action commits its own write (its own super::atomic / tasks::create / knowledge::create on an autocommit connection), and the automation_runs INSERT is a separate atomic at 2694-2701; a failed insert leaves no run row so `due` stays true (2795-2798) and the action repeats each tick. evidence: `let (num, unit) = rest.split_at(rest.len() - 1);` is a byte index; for "every: 5м" (Cyrillic) or an Armenian unit it lands inside a code point and str::split_at panics. It is called from run_due_halves (2782), which lib.rs:460 runs under state.db.lock(), so the panic poisons the mutex.

verify: repo.rs:2725 is `rest.split_at(rest.len() - 1)`, a byte index; for '5м' (len 3) index 2 is inside the two-byte char and str::split_at panics, and the caller chain run_due_halves (2782) runs under state.db.lock() in lib.rs:459-462. Read, not executed (cargo forbidden); only enabled automations reach the parse and nothing in the shipped app can arm one (finding 0, create() inserts enabled=0), so latent and low today.

evidence: `"m" => Some(n * 60_000), "h" => Some(n * 3_600_000), "d" => Some(n * 86_400_000)` with n any positive i64 parsed from a trigger of up to 500 chars; a large n panics in debug and wraps in release, and a negative interval makes `>= interval` always true (2796).

I did not locate the 500-char cap; the overflow does not depend on it. Not recorded.

evidence: `for a in list(conn)? {` returns from run_due_halves at once. Doc 2755-2757: "Each due automation and the agent half are now attempted regardless"; 2843-2845: "it no longer depends on the automation half above having succeeded". The test at 3631 breaks exactly this table.

evidence: `let id = format!("fr-{}-{}", &digest[..12], now_ms);` panics if the stored digest is shorter than 12 bytes. register (2953) and set_active (2980) accept any string as `digest`, and migration 0025 puts no length CHECK on bundle_digest.

evidence: pending = `status = 'pending'` (4524); decided = `status IN ('approved','rejected','consumed')` (4528). An `escalated` row (set at 1063, with "no way out" per 1055) falls out of both headline counts.

verify: refuse_corrupt (supervisor_ledger.rs:994-998) tests only `feh.len() != 64`, EvidenceHead::validate (:896-898) also requires hex digits, and supervisor_ledger.sql:174 is `TEXT NOT NULL` with no CHECK. A non-hex row can only arrive by direct database tampering, hence low.

evidence: `for cap in 0..=63i32 { unsafe { libc::prctl(libc::PR_CAPBSET_DROP, ...); } }` discards the return; the method returns only the ambient-clear result. Doc at 1007-1010 says a step is recorded `the moment the corresponding method returns true`. The comment also cites a `capget-verify`; the check is a /proc/self/status parse.

evidence: `Err(_) if !path.exists() => 0,` — a second, symlink-following path lookup. A dangling symlink at the counter path fails the O_NOFOLLOW open and `exists()` is false, so the counter restarts; the doc (617-619) says `a damaged one is an error ... rather than a silent restart, because restarting is indistinguishable from a rollback`.
suggested_fix: Decide 'missing' from the open's own errno (ENOENT only) instead of a second path lookup.
title: Head-sequence counter silently restarts at 1 on any open error where `path.exists()` is false
verify: governed_recorder.rs:642 is `Err(_) if !path.exists() => 0`, a symlink-following second lookup after read_measured's O_NOFOLLOW open, so a dangling symlink restarts the counter at 1 against the doc at 617-619. Low: the directory is checked recorder-private first (628-630), so only the recorder uid or root could plant it.

evidence: `let mut status: i32 = 0; unsafe { libc::waitpid(pid, &mut status, 0); } let exit_code = if libc::WIFEXITED(status) { libc::WEXITSTATUS(status) } else { -1 };` — if waitpid returns -1, status stays 0, WIFEXITED(0) is true and exit_code is 0, so `produced` depends only on the pipe bytes.
suggested_fix: Check `waitpid(..) == pid` (retrying EINTR) and treat any other return as a refusal.
title: `waitpid` result is unchecked; a failed wait reads as exit code 0
verify: governed_recorder.rs:826-830: waitpid's return is discarded and status starts at 0, so a failed wait gives WIFEXITED(0) true and exit_code 0; `produced` (835) then rests only on the pipe bytes. Read, not run.

evidence: `write_json`: `if let Ok(text) = ... { let _ = std::fs::write(path, text.as_bytes()); }`; `record_line`: `if let Ok(mut fh) = OpenOptions...open(path) { let _ = writeln!(fh, "{value}"); }`. `finish` (622-625) then returns 0 on `matched` regardless of whether ladder-turn.json was written.

title: Evidence writers swallow every I/O error, so a run can exit 0 with no evidence on disk
verify: write_json (218-222) and record_line (224-229) discard every serialise, open and write error, and finish (622-625) returns 0 on `matched` without checking that ladder-turn.json was written.

evidence: `match s(&cfg, &["trust", "manifest_sig_path"]).and_then(|p| std::fs::read_to_string(p).ok()) { ... None => return setup_blocked(&evidence, expect, "manifest_sig_unreadable", &manifest_path)` — the detail is the manifest's path, and an absent `trust.manifest_sig_path` is not reported as `config_missing` like every sibling key.

evidence: L592-604 and L881-889 accept only 'e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::PermissionDenied'; every other error returns writable(..., 'custody cannot be measured'). File::create on a read-only mount fails EROFS (ReadOnlyFilesystem), not EACCES, including the walk through '/' and '/var'. By reading, not run.

I reproduced the errno in a private mount namespace: O_CREAT on a read-only tmpfs returns EROFS, not EACCES, and no ReadOnlyFilesystem/EROFS handling exists anywhere under provision/src. Fail-closed, so an availability defect only.

evidence: mint_floor_anchor (1033) and mint_control_room_command (1081, 1091) return `corrupt(..)` for a bad head_sequence/expiry/empty field. Corrupt's Display (360-369) prints 'the provisioned trust store is not usable ... an ADMINISTRATOR removes the trust anchor directory'.

title: Argument-validation failures are reported as a corrupt trust store

A wrong error class for a caller's argument.

evidence: 1436 `anchor_dir.join(MANIFEST_FILE).is_file()`, 1461 `anchor_dir.exists()`, 1661 `!trust.exists()`. Lines 1344-1349 of the same file: '`Path::exists()` answers `false` for every error ... read as "no signer"'. posix_install.rs:561 says is_file is the wrong question for a manifest.
suggested_fix: Use symlink_metadata and classify only NotFound as absent, as custody_record_from_read and settle_existing do.
title: The idempotency and occupancy checks use is_file()/exists(), which answer false for every error — the defect this file fixed for the custody record
verify: lib.rs:1436 uses `.is_file()`, :1461 `anchor_dir.exists()`, :1661 `!trust.exists()` (and :2218 is_file again), while :1344-1349 of the same file explains why exists() answering false for every error was a defect and posix_install.rs:561-569 uses symlink_metadata for the same question. Consequence read through: a stat error falls to a later refusal or failed write, so low.

evidence: `let stem = name.strip_suffix(".json").unwrap_or(&name); if !RETAINED_AUTHORITIES.contains(&stem)` — an entry named `builder` (no .json, file or directory) has stem "builder" and passes, though the mint never wrote it and no digest covers it.
